Online Stopwatch with Laps and Full Screen | Saat Tarih
Free online stopwatch: lap times, best and slowest lap, full screen and keyboard shortcuts. Your time is kept even if you reload the page.
The stopwatch is accurate to a hundredth of a second, records lap times and keeps your time even if you reload or close and reopen the page. Space starts and stops it, L adds a lap.
Shortcuts: Space start/stop, L lap, R reset.
Countdown Timer: By Duration or Date | Saat Tarih
Free countdown: a minute timer or the time left until a date you choose. Countdown to New Year and bayram, sound alert and full screen.

The countdown works in two ways: a timer that alerts you when your chosen duration ends, or a live display of the days, hours and seconds left until a date you pick. Count down to New Year, a bayram or your own date.
Enter a valid duration or a date in the future.
You can share the link for the date you picked; the countdown starts by itself when the link is opened.
Online Alarm Clock: Repeating and Snooze | Saat Tarih
Free alarm that runs in your browser: time, label, repeat on chosen weekdays, 5-minute snooze and notifications. The alarm rings while the page is open.

Choose an alarm time and the days you want; when the time comes a sound plays and a notification appears. Alarms are stored on this device. Because of browser limits, the alarm only rings while this page (tab) stays open.
If the screen turns off the browser may put the tab to sleep; this option stops the screen from turning off while an alarm is set.
For important wake-ups also set your phone\'s own alarm; a browser alarm will not ring if the page is closed.
Pomodoro Timer: Work 25 Minutes, Break 5 | Saat Tarih
Free pomodoro timer: 25 minutes of work, a 5-minute short break and a long break every 4 rounds. Adjustable times, sound alerts and full screen.
The Pomodoro technique alternates 25 minutes of focused work with 5-minute short breaks, followed by a long break after 4 rounds. The times can be changed and a sound plays at each switch.
Date Calculator: Days, Working Days, Age | Saat Tarih
How many days and working days between two dates? Add or subtract days, months or years from a date and calculate age. Turkish public holidays are taken into account.

Calculate the days, weeks and working days between two dates; add days, months, years or working days to a date; and find your age and next birthday. Working-day counts leave out weekends and Turkish public holidays.
Working days leave out weekends and public holidays; bayram eve half days count as 0.5.

How far along is the season?

Earth travels once around the Sun every year. But it doesn\'t stand up straight: its axis is tilted 23.4 degrees, always the same way. For half the year the northern half leans toward the Sun and it\'s summer; for the other half it leans away and it\'s winter.
A common mix-up: seasons don\'t happen because we get closer to or farther from the Sun. Earth is closest to the Sun in early January – right in our winter!

In summer the Sun is high in the sky; its rays hit the ground straight on and warm a small patch well. In winter the Sun is low; the same light spreads over a bigger area and warms it less. Winter days are also short, so the ground has less time to warm up.
Does winter start on December 1 or December 21?

Both are right, because there are two ways to count. Astronomers start a season by the Sun\'s position: winter begins on the longest night (December 21, the winter solstice). Meteorologists (weather scientists) use whole months to keep their numbers simple: December, January and February are winter. That\'s why some calendars say “winter starts on December 1”.
Flipped on the other half of the world
While we have winter, it\'s summer in Australia, South Africa and Argentina. Kids there often celebrate New Year on the beach!
June 21 is the longest day of the year and December 21 the longest night (in the northern half).
On the equinoxes in March and September, day and night are almost equal.
At the North Pole the Sun doesn\'t set for months in summer, and doesn\'t rise for months in winter.
Near the equator summer and winter feel almost the same; instead there are rainy and dry seasons.
In the northern half, summer is a few days longer than winter: Earth moves a little slower when it\'s farther from the Sun.
